result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.cmty_l_eigenvec()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Detect communities using Leading Eigenvector (Newman) algorithm. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L13650-L13768){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.cmty_l_eigenvec( attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Spectral optimization method using recursive bisection based on the leading eigenvector of the modularity matrix. Splits communities hierarchically when modularity improves. Best for medium-sized graphs (< 20K nodes) with clear 2-way divisions and hierarchical structure. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Column name to store community assignments in the node DataFrame. If `None` (default), automatically uses `cmty_l_eigenvec`. Overwrites column if it already exists. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores in NDF and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, int], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to community IDs (0-indexed, contiguous). If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If graph is directed (requires undirected graph). ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Newman (2006) recast community detection as a linear-algebra problem: the modularity matrix $B_{ij} = A_{ij} - \dfrac{k_i k_j}{2m}$ measures each edge's contribution to modularity relative to a null model, and its leading eigenvector defines the split that gains the most modularity in one binary cut. The implementation finds that eigenvector by power iteration, partitions nodes by sign, and recurses on each side, refusing to split whenever doing so would lower modularity. Each split costs $O(n^2)$, and the recursion terminates only when the structure genuinely has hierarchical two-way divisions, so the final community count can be smaller than what agglomerative methods produce. Use `cmty_fast_greedy()` or `cmty_louvain()` beyond a few tens of thousands of nodes. ## Examples {.doc-examples} The eigenvector split finds the natural division at the bridge edge, giving each triangle its own community: ::: {#da15b9fd .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_node(label="E") .add_node(label="F") ) # Build two complete triangles for i, j in [("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A")]: graph.add_edge(i, j) graph.add_edge("C", "D") # Bridge for i, j in [("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")]: graph.add_edge(i, j) communities = graph.cmty_l_eigenvec(return_dict=True) {graph.get_label_from_id(nid): cid for nid, cid in communities.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'C': 0, 'A': 0, 'E': 1, 'F': 1, 'D': 1, 'B': 0} ``` ::: ::: Storing the result as a node attribute and chaining into `colorize_node_attrs()` visualizes the communities directly: ::: {#c85ac16d .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_node(label="E") .add_node(label="F") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") .add_edge(source="B", target="C") .add_edge(source="C", target="A") .add_edge(source="C", target="D") .add_edge(source="D", target="E") .add_edge(source="E", target="F") .add_edge(source="F", target="D") ) ( graph .cmty_l_eigenvec(attr_name="community") .colorize_node_attrs(node_attr_from="community", palette="Spectral") .describe() ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Number of nodes : 6 Number of edges : 7 Directed : False Density : 0.47 Average degree (min, max) : 2.33 (2, 3) Connected : True Number of connected components : 1 Tree : False Bipartite : False Computations on nodes: - cmty_l_eigenvec() -> attr: 'community' (6 of 6 nodes) Node aesthetics: - color <- community via colorize (palette: "Spectral") (values: #d53e4f, #f46d43, 6 of 6 nodes) ``` ::: :::
